newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 24.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5649. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Conflicts over the ruling New Korea Party's planned reorganization are becoming evident within the party ahead of President Kim Young-sam's scheduled public statement on Tuesday.
- South Korea's 1998 national college-entrance examination for high school seniors will be held on November 19, the Ministry of Education said on Sunday.

- U.S. Secretary of State, Madeleine Albright, during her first visit to South Korea over the weekend, reaffirmed U.S. commitment to the nation and stressed the need for Seoul's adherence to U.S. policy on North Korea.
- Opposition parties on Sunday demanded that Kim Hyun-chul, second son of President Kim Young-sam, take the stand for a planned national assembly hearing into the Hanbo loan scandal. -----
- About ten formerly militant trade unions including Ssangyong Motors and Hyosung Heavy Industries, are showing signs of veering from the war path in efforts to help revive the companies.
